anomalies.observed: The net named USBC_D_N contains the USB-C D- pins J3.A7 and J3.B7, and also contains all ground pins including U25.2, U25.4, U26.2, U26.4, and Module1 GND pins. This shorts the USB-C D- line to ground.
anomalies.expected: USB-C D- should be a separate signal net connected to the USB mux and ESD protection, not tied to the ground net.

evidence.quote: USBC_D_N : ... J3.A7(D-,bidirectional) J3.B7(D-,bidirectional) ... U25.2(GND,passive) U25.4(I/O2,passive) U26.2(GND,passive) U26.4(I/O2,passive) ...

anomalies.impact: The USB-C port's D- line is shorted to ground, making USB-C data communication impossible.

anomalies.observed: The I2C/~SPI mode select pins U13.9 and U14.9 are tied to GND, selecting I2C mode, but the rest of the connections (pins 10-13) are wired for SPI mode and pin 14 (SDA/VSS) is also tied to GND.
anomalies.expected: For SPI mode, U13.9 and U14.9 should be tied to +3V3. For I2C mode, pin 14 should be SDA, not grounded.

evidence.quote: U13.9(I2C/~{SPI},input) ... U14.9(I2C/~{SPI},input) ... GND net includes U13.14(SDA/VSS,bidirectional) U14.14(SDA/VSS,bidirectional)

anomalies.impact: The SC16IS752 UARTs are configured for I2C mode but have their SDA pins grounded and SPI signals on other pins, so they will not function.

parsed.summary: The design files contain at least two serious anomalies: the USB-C D- line is shorted to ground via the USBC_D_N net, and the SC16IS752 UARTs have their mode select pins tied low while wired for SPI, rendering them non-functional.
